Date: 2025-01-09
REMARKS
In this response, claims 1, 4, 8-9, and 16 have been amended. Supports for the amendments can
be found from the specification and the drawings as originally filed. No new matter is added by the present amendment and response. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of
these claims in view of the above amendments and the following remarks.
As Applicant's remarks with respect to the Examiner's rejections are seen as sufficient to
overcome these rejections, Applicant's silence as to assertions by the Examiner in the Office Action or certain requirements that may be applicable to such rejections (for example, assertions regarding dependent claims, whether a reference constitutes prior art, and whether references are legally combinable for obviousness purposes) is not a concession by Applicant that such assertions are
accurate or such requirements have been met, and Applicant reserves the right to analyze and dispute
such in the future.
Claim Reiections - 35 U.S.C. 112
The Office Action indicates that claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35
U.S.C. 112, because claims 1, 9, and 16 recite the limitation "outward refraction of the sightline" and
"final gaze point of the sightline" that has no sufficient antecedent basis.
In response, Applicant has made appropriate amendments to claims 1, 9, and 16 to overcome the
above rejections.
Claim Rejections - 35 USC 101
The Office Action recites that claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the claims
are directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the opinion and traverses as follows.
Reg. ardingf amended claim 1:
Amended claim 1 recites a method for visually tracking a gaze point of a human eye. The
amended claim I is directed to a process, which is one of the statutory categories of invention.
The present application as recited in amended claim 1 refers to the automobile control technical
field and includes the limitation of "in response that a match between the host vehicle and a visual
tracking device is established, the host vehicle calculating a distance between a centroid of the host
vehicle and the visual tracking device; in response that the distance is determined to be less than or equal to a preset distance, the host vehicle periodically receiving position coordinates of a human eye of a driver of the host vehicle and coordinates of a gaze point of a sightline of the human eye on an inner side of a current projection screen, provided by the visual tracking device; and the host vehicle screening out a refractive index and a curvature of the current projection screen, and combining with
the position coordinates of the human eye and the coordinates of the gaze point of the sightline on the inner side of the current projection screen, obtaining coordinates of a gaze point of the sightline on an outer side of the current projection screen and a corresponding refracted light path formed by outward
refraction of a sightline, and further combining with a preset normal viewing distance of the human eye, obtaining a final gaze point of a sightline on the corresponding refracted light path and
coordinates of the final gaze point".
The above limitations refer to tracking the final gaze point of the driver of the host vehicle. In detail, as claimed in amended claim 1, the present application determines the coordinates of the final gaze point of the driver according to data, e.g., the position coordinates of the human eye of the driver and coordinates of the gaze point of the sightline of the human eye on the inner side of the projection screen that are received from the visual tracking device. Specially, in response that a match between the host vehicle and the visual tracking device has been established, a distance between the centroid of the host vehicle and the visual tracking device is calculated. Under
the condition that the distance is less than or equal to the preset distance, the data, e.g., the position coordinates of the human eye of the driver and the coordinates of the gaze point of the sightline of the human eye on the inner side of the projection screen are received. Applicant submits that amended claim 1 at least recites additional elements that integrate a judicial exception into a practical application.
In addition, as mentioned above, under the condition that the distance between the centroid of
the host vehicle and the visual tracking device is less than or equal to the preset distance, the data, e.g., the position coordinates of the human eye of the driver and the coordinates of the gaze point of the sightline of the human eye on the inner side of the projection screen provided by the visual tracking device are received and used for determining the coordinates of the final gaze point of the driver, so
as to realize the tracking of the final gaze point of the driver. Accordingly, the data as mentioned above can ensure the accuracy of positioning the final gaze point of the driver. In detail, in the automobile control technology, there may be more than one visual tracking devices installed on the vehicle to assist in monitoring a driving safety of the vehicle. Different visual tracking devices may be installed on different positions of the vehicle. It should be noted that, as recited in amended claim 1, under the condition that the distance between the centroid of the host vehicle and the visual tracking device is less than or equal to the preset distance, these data used for determining the coordinates of the final gaze point of the driver are received. Therefore, it ensures the accuracy of these received data. Accordingly, the accuracy of the coordinates of the final gaze point of the driver determined according to these received data can be ensured. Thus, the present application of amended claim L
makes an improvement to the automobile control technology field.
Based on the above analysis, Applicant submits that amended claim 1 is eligible. Thus,
dependent claims of the amended claim l are also eligible.
Regardingr amended claim 9:
Amended claim 9 recites a vehicle early warning method. The amended claim 9 is directed to
a process, which is one of the statutory categories of invention.
The present application as recited in amended claim 9 recites the limitation of "the host vehicle
periodically receiving position coordinates of a human eye of a driver of the host vehicle and coordinates of a gaze point of a sightline of the human eye on an inner side of a current projection
screen, provided by a visual tracking device; wherein, the current projection screen is a windshield or a front window of the host vehicle; the host vehicle screening out a refractive index and a curvature of the current projection screen, and combining with the position coordinates of the human eye and the coordinates of the gaze point of the sightline on the inner side of the current projection screen, obtaining coordinates of a gaze point of the sightline on an outer side of the current projection screen and a corresponding refracted light path formed by outward refraction of a sightline, and further combining with a preset normal viewing distance of the human eye, obtaining a final gaze point of a sightline on the corresponding refracted light path and coordinates of the final gaze point; the host vehicle acquiring vehicle information of a distant vehicle within a predetermined period, and acquiring vehicle information of the host vehicle, and a fatigue state of the driver of the host vehicle; according
to the vehicle information of the distant vehicle and the vehicle information of the host vehicle, the coordinates of the final gaze point of the sightline, and the fatigue state of the driver of the host vehicle, the host vehicle detecting whether a motion trajectory of the distant vehicle and the sightline intersect, and detecting whether the distant vehicle and the final gaze point of the sightline are located in a same relative azimuth area of the host vehicle and detecting a fatigue degree of the driver of the host vehicle,
and according to detection results, the host vehicle determining a warning level of a collision between the host vehicle and the distant vehicle; and the host vehicle generating early warning information according to the warning level and sending the early warning infornation to the driver of the host
vehicle".
The above limitations above refer to providing a warning to the driver of the host vehicle timely
once a warning level of a collision is determined. In detail, as claimed in the amended claim 9, the present application tracks the final gaze point of the driver by determining the coordinates of the final gaze point of the driver using those data such as the position coordinates of the human eye of the driver and the coordinates of the gaze point of the sightline of the human eye on the inner side of the projection screen received from the visual tracking device; then determining the warning level of the collision between the host vehicle and the distant vehicle according to detection results including a detection result of whether a motion trajectory of the distant vehicle and the sightline intersect determined based on the final gaze point; and then sending the early warning information corresponding to the warning level to the driver of the host vehicle. That is, the present application links the processes of tracking the final gaze point to the motion trajectory of the distant vehicle, which
cannot be done without a device. In other words, the present application cannot be done in the mind,
and it does not fall within the "mental process" grouping of the abstract idea.
In addition, in the automobile control technology filed, no prior art recites that the processes of
tracking the final gaze point are linked to the motion trajectory of the distant vehicle. Furthermore, as the early warning information corresponding to the warning level can be sent to the driver of the
host vehicle once the warning level of collision between the host vehicle and the distant vehicle is determined under the link of tracking the final gaze point to the motion trajectory of the distant vehicle, the present application ensures the driving security, and makes an improvement to the automobile
control technology filed.
Based on the above analysis, Applicant submits that the amended claim 9 is also eligible.
Amended claim 16 recites features similar to claim 9. Therefore, amended claim 9 and dependent
claims of the amended claims 9 and L6 are also eligible.
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection to claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C.101
be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Allowable Subiect Matter
The Office Action states that claims 1-20 would be allowable if rewritten or amended to
overcome the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101, set forth in this Office action.
In response, Applicant respectfully appreciates the careful examination on the present
application. Applicant has made appropriate amendments to overcome the above 35 U.S.C. 10l
rejections. Therefore, independent claims 1, 9, and 16 and their dependent claims are allowable.
CONCLUSION
This application is in condition for allowance and a Notice to that effect is earnestly solicited.
If the Examiner believes that there are any issues that can be resolved by a telephone conference, or that there are any informalities that can be corrected by an Examiner's amendment, please call the undersigned at the number given below.
The undersigned representative requests any extension of time that may be deemed necessary to
further the prosecution of this application.
The undersigned representative authorizes the Commissioner to charge any additional fees under 37 C.F.R. 1.16 or 1.17 that may be required, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No.
5051 42, referencing Attorney Docket No.: US87146.
